We now have two versions of the MCP read-only access; one with principals, and one with sessions we control with a hook. (Ref at https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/Eg4aD33rW )
Now, I see a new supabase page that may give a third way: Scoped personal access tokens. https://supabase.com/changelog/scoped-personal-access-tokens-ga and https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/personal-access-tokens . Looks good, but I mostly see UI access to create tokens, not sure we could do it through the api on behalf of users, can you check?

input.prompt: What are scoped personal access tokens? What do they grant access to (Management API, database data, PostgREST)? Can they be created via API, OAuth, or on behalf of other users? Quote relevant passages verbatim.

result.output:
**What they are:** Scoped PATs are tokens limited to chosen projects or organizations, with only the permissions you select. The page says, "You can limit a token to specific projects or organizations and grant only the permissions it needs." At creation you choose resources, permissions, and expiry, up to one year out.

**What they grant:**
- **Management API:** The page says "all `/v1` and `/v2` endpoints." A 403 response lists the missing permissions in a `missing_permissions` array.
- **MCP server and CLI:** Each MCP tool checks the token's permissions. The CLI accepts scoped tokens through `supabase login --token` or `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`.
- **Database data:** The page only covers SQL. It says "SQL runs read-only unless the token has Database read-write." Access to secret API keys requires the API Key Secrets permission.
- **PostgREST:** The page doesn't mention PostgREST.

**Creation methods:** Tokens are created on the access tokens page in the dashboard. The page doesn't say whether they can be created via API or OAuth, or on behalf of other users.

**Other limits:** A token's access can't be changed after creation, and "A token never has more access than you do." Existing account-level tokens keep working, and "Create legacy token" is still available.

input.prompt: How are personal access tokens created (UI, API endpoint, CLI)? What do scopes cover — Management API only, or database/PostgREST data access? Can they be created on behalf of end users of a project? Any mention of OAuth apps or Management API endpoints for tokens? Quote verbatim.

content.text:
Short answer: no. And the bigger problem isn't the API. These tokens belong to the wrong kind of user.

**What they are.** Personal access tokens are for Supabase *platform* accounts: the developers who sign in to supabase.com and manage projects. They authenticate to the Management API (`/v1`, `/v2`) and the tools built on it, which are the CLI and Supabase's own MCP server. The new scopes narrow a token to certain projects or orgs and certain Management API permissions. Neither page mentions PostgREST or our project's Auth users.

**Creating them through the API.** The docs describe only two ways to make one:
- the dashboard's access-tokens settings page;
- `supabase login`, which makes a token with your account's full access.

Neither page lists an endpoint for creating tokens, an OAuth flow for minting them, or any way to issue one for another person. "A token never has more access than you do" means it is always tied to the Supabase account that created it.

**Why that rules it out for us.** Our Discourse Graph users are Auth users inside our project. They have no supabase.com accounts, and we wouldn't want them to. Even if we could mint a token for someone, all it could do is let them manage our project's infrastructure, not read their own space's data under row-level security. For data access, the closest it gets is read-only SQL through the Management API. That runs as a privileged database role, not as the user, so our RLS would not apply.

Supabase does have OAuth apps for platform integrations ("Build a Supabase Integration"), but those also act on behalf of Supabase account holders, so the same mismatch applies.

So this isn't a third option next to principals and hook-controlled sessions. It could only help with our team's own tooling, like giving an agent a read-only, single-project token for running migrations or checking the advisor, instead of a full-access token.

I checked only the two pages you linked. I didn't search the Management API reference for undocumented token endpoints, and I didn't open the Roam page, since the answer doesn't depend on its details. I can do either if you want.

Sources:
- [Scoped personal access tokens GA](https://supabase.com/changelog/scoped-personal-access-tokens-ga)
- [Personal access tokens docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/personal-access-tokens)
Ah, ok, thanks for correcting me.
